cases.prompt: I added two libraries to pom.xml for the depot catalog import. Before this goes any further, are any of our dependencies known to be vulnerable?
I staged a reports service and its controller; no dependency changed. Review that code for security holes before I merge it: injection, broken authorization and data the endpoints expose.
I staged the catalog import from the regional depot, with two new libraries in pom.xml. Check the dependencies and the new code for vulnerabilities and tell me what has to be fixed before merging.
cases.review: The answer lists each step of the chain (the dependency-check plugin is not in pom.xml, OSV-Scanner and the dependency-check CLI cannot run here) with the exact command to run, and says that the dependency findings are manual until a scanner confirms them. It reports log4j-core 2.14.1 (pom.xml:52) as CVE-2021-44228, Critical, fixed in 2.17.1 or later, and commons-text 1.9 (pom.xml:47) as CVE-2022-42889, Critical, fixed in 1.10.0, both as A03:2025 Software Supply Chain Failures and introduced by this change. It marks both as reachable from the X-Depot header: the interpolator at CatalogImportController.java:26 and the log call at line 27. It reports the ObjectInputStream on the request body (lines 28-29) as unsafe deserialization, CWE-502, A08:2025, Critical. Every finding has an OWASP Top 10:2025 category with its year, the Critical findings are listed for verify, nothing was installed and no file was changed.
